title: Compose UI from constrained utilities
principle: Adam Wathan’s Tailwind/public teaching: style by composing a constrained utility vocabulary rather than inventing open-ended CSS per component. Distinct from Refactoring UI visual tips (already on Schoger)—this is about the composition model that keeps AI from emitting unbounded stylesheets.
procedure: Give the agent your utility/token vocabulary (spacing scale, type scale, colors).
Require class/composition output inside that vocabulary—no arbitrary values unless justified.
Extract repeated compositions into components only after they stabilize.
Review diffs for arbitrary value creep ([13px], [#a1b2c3]).
examplePrompts:
Implement this card utility-first (Wathan / Tailwind public model):
- Use only the project spacing/type/color scales.
- No arbitrary values unless you justify with a one-line why.
- Extract a component only if the composition repeats ≥3 times.
Return markup + any extraction.
Audit this AI stylesheet for arbitrary values; remap to the scale or delete.
promptWhy: Vocabulary constraint is the whole point vs freehand CSS.
Arbitrary-value audit catches AI ‘close enough’ pixels.
tips: Visual hierarchy tips live under Steve Schoger techniques—don’t duplicate.

workedExamples.title: Premature extract
workedExamples.body: Two similar cards stay composed; third repeat earns a component.

antiPatterns: Open-ended CSS beside a utility system.
checklist: Scale vocabulary provided to the agent.
